selected_primary_sources.project_relevance: Grouped fingerprints considered; do not by themselves remove complete-array growth.
Separate logical clear from memory release; project instead predicts capacity without retaining empty arrays.
Bound each table growth with extendible hashing; scale and bookkeeping differ from tiny batches.
Direct integer mapping without full-array copying; sparse high IDs and page costs require scrutiny.
Generation/index identifiers and retention constraints do not directly match existing monotonic IDs.
Multiply-shift has explicit random-family assumptions; cheaper hashing alone is not a universal optimum.
Counterexamples constrain low-independence linear-probing claims.
Explicit placement new avoids relying on later union-copy lifetime wording in C++17.
Review explicit activation of lazy union payloads and inactive-member access.
Review old union-copy object representation wording.
Sharding and temporal locality studied; replacing the process allocator is outside this internal optimization.
Cross-thread free batching studied; no new allocator dependency or thread-local ownership restriction introduced.
Frontend batching informs fixed-cost analysis; unchanged public ownership and budget paths remain necessary.
Phase-oriented storage informs lifecycle separation; leases and uncertain callbacks still require explicit tracking.
Scope cleanup and shared versus confined ownership inform ergonomic wrapper contracts.
Callback-scoped temporary allocation informs one-line lifetime-safe usage.
RAII cleanup must hold through normal completion and exceptions.
Arena reset and capacity-release separation considered; project retains no empty metadata arrays.
Incremental growth considered; amortized and peak costs still need project-specific measurement.
Intrusive links replace external node bookkeeping; actual object lifetime remains explicitly owned.
Two links per node and a two-pointer empty container suffice for the required operations.
Clear link state explicitly on removal; validate linkage invariants through targeted tests.
Automatic destructor unlinking can mutate unsynchronized containers; project avoids this behavior.
Separate unlinking from object disposal and provider/resource cleanup.
Link mutation must remain serialized by the existing domain mutex.
